questions.prompt: Explain what ConfigureAwait(false) changes about an await, where it matters, and how it relates to the classic .Result / .Wait() deadlock.

keyPoints.text: The STEP 1 call awaits GetStringAsync with ConfigureAwait(false) appended.
It tells the await not to capture the current SynchronizationContext for the continuation.
That matters most in library code and ASP.NET code.
Blocking on async code with .Result or .Wait() is a production deadlock source.
keyPoints.quote: Deadlocks from blocking on async code ( .Result / .Wait() ).

keyPoints.text: Capturing the context when you do not need it is listed as its own pitfall.
The beginner lesson already warns that .Result or .Wait() can deadlock.

questions.prompt: Walk through how a CancellationToken should flow through an async method like ProcessAsync, and what goes wrong when it does not.

keyPoints.text: The method accepts a token with a default value, so callers that cannot cancel may omit it.
keyPoints.quote: public async Task ProcessAsync(CancellationToken ct = default)

keyPoints.text: The token is passed into the HTTP call so the I/O itself can be cancelled.
Between steps the method checks the token and throws if cancellation was requested.
The rule of thumb is to always pass the token along.
Not passing or checking the token is a common production pitfall.
The async bug hunt lists not using CancellationToken among the hardest async bugs.

questions.prompt: Explain async cleanup with await using / IAsyncDisposable and how it fits the junior challenge of a resilient parallel async method.

keyPoints.text: STEP 3 disposes a resource asynchronously with await using.
keyPoints.quote: await using var resource = new AsyncResource();

keyPoints.text: IAsyncDisposable is for resources whose cleanup is itself asynchronous.
keyPoints.quote: Use IAsyncDisposable for resources that have async cleanup.

keyPoints.text: Forgetting to await or dispose async resources is a production pitfall.
keyPoints.quote: Forgetting to await or dispose async resources.

keyPoints.text: The challenge asks for two external calls running in parallel.
keyPoints.quote: Calls two external services in parallel

keyPoints.text: It must clean up on every failure path, not just the happy path.
keyPoints.quote: Cleans up properly on any failure path

keyPoints.text: Parallel calls start each task first and then await them together with Task.WhenAll, as in the beginner lesson.
